text:
mike: Heads-up — GreenCart reporting spikes of 429s + occasional 500s on their Dedicated pool. They say it feels like churn, scale up/down every couple minutes.
priya: I pulled the autoscaler logs, same. Rapid scale-up then almost-immediate scale-down. Provision time ~40-50s, cooldown is 60s right now.
alvaro: Support attached trace: spike -> 429s -> scale up -> error rate drops -> scale down -> repeat. Customer says this began after enabling a burst routing rule yesterday.
kevin-support: Confirmed: routing-policy change at 2026-03-13T09:12:00Z to allow burst traffic to dedicated. Their traffic pattern is heavy tails (short aggressive bursts).
jess: Can someone paste the current autoscaler policy for pool-greencart and the recent metric window? Need smoothing and target thresholds.
sre-bot: autoscaler/getPolicy --id=pool-greencart
sre-bot: policy: target_cpu=65, target_queue_len=30, cooldown=60s, min_replicas=1, max_replicas=12, smoothing_window=30s
mike: Short snippet from scale log around spike:
```
[09:14:23] scale_up -> replicas=2 (trigger: queue_len=38)
[09:16:12] scale_down -> replicas=1 (cooldown elapsed)
[09:18:05] scale_up -> replicas=2 (trigger: cpu=78)
[09:19:40] scale_down -> replicas=1
```
priya: With provision ~45s, a burst causes single replica to be saturated while a new one boots; queued requests hit 429s. cooldown 60s + smoothing 30s means we will often oscillate for short repeating bursts.
alvaro: Node telemetry shows noisy-neighbor CPU spikes on node-67 at 09:15 that aggravated the first trigger — single replica got hit harder.
jess: Support repro steps provided: set tenant routing -> dedicated, then run burst script: 500 RPS for 20s, idle 40s, repeat. They can reproduce reliably.
kevin-support: Repro script snippet they used:
```
for i in {1..10}; do hey -n 10000 -c 500 http://greencart.dedicated/api/generate; sleep 40; done
```
mike: Immediate mitigation suggestions:
- increase cooldown -> 180s and smoothing_window -> 90s
- set min_replicas=2 for this pool to avoid single-rep bottleneck
- pre-warm a small standby set when burst routing is enabled
- client-side: add 429->retry with jitter/backoff to reduce request storm
priya: I'll push a quick config to staging: cooldown=180, smoothing=90, min_replicas=2, watch for 30-60m.
jess: Also recommend disabling tenant-level burst routing for GreenCart until we confirm tuning. Reduces risk of thrash.
alvaro: Longer term: switch autoscaler to rate-aware logic (e.g., p95 queue_len over 60s) and detect noisy neighbor outliers from node metrics. Could also add per-node affinity to reduce co-tenancy bursts.
kevin-support: Told customer we'll run tests and follow up in an hour. They're okay with temporary min_replicas=2, prefer no downtime.
mike: Action items:
- priya: deploy staging config and run their repro in 10m
- alvaro: deep-dive node-67 docker logs + pod placement for noisy neighbor
- jess: prepare quick rollback for autoscaler config (current values saved)
- kevin-support: coordinate with GreenCart, capture before/after traces and token errors
priya: Deploy kicked off to staging, tagging @oncall.
sre-bot: deploy/autoscaler-config staging pool-greencart --cooldown=180 --smoothing=90 --min_replicas=2
sre-bot: deploy started
mike: If staging looks good we can schedule prod change in off-peak window (customer ok with 02:00 UTC maintenance).
jess: Also let's create an alert: if scale actions > 3 in 10m for a pool -> page SRE. That will catch flapping automatically.
alvaro: Opening a follow-up ticket to propose metric changes and include node telemetry. Will attach noisy-neighbor findings.
kevin-support: Customer sent logs showing token/timeouts during the scale events; adding to case.
mike: Keeping this thread as the runbook for triage and for the postmortem notes. Update here with staging results.
